answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and 14-day renewal deadline create pressure, but the 94% line utilization and critical-path dependency rule out switching to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2 showed SLA misses in 3/4 quarters). Adding a second source would help resilience but not meet the cost target alone. Negotiating_terms with the incumbent offers the highest probability of cost recovery while preserving stability: memory_c4 demonstrated renegotiation at renewal recovered real margin and moved the incumbent on price and terms; memory_c6 showed multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing. A standard experiment posture (renegotiate firmly but with fallback to renewal if needed) preserves the option to defer if terms don't move sufficiently, protecting against delivery interruption on day 14. Verification of memory_c4 and memory_c2 will confirm the incumbent's historical flexibility and the cost/risk profile of alternatives.
